instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines "legislative agent" by purpose ("as one of the individual's main purposes") and requires registration within ten days of engagement without specifying any minimum compensation dollar threshold.
Registration is required within ten days following an engagement of a legislative agent, with no expenditure dollar threshold triggering the registration obligation.

Itemized disclosure of meals and food/beverage expenditures to a particular official is required only when cumulative payments to that official during the calendar year exceed a total of fifty dollars.
Registered legislative agents and employers must file expenditure statements showing total expenditures with no de minimis dollar threshold exempting them from the filing obligation itself.
The expenditure-statement filing obligation under §101.73 applies to all registered legislative agents and employers without any time-percent de minimis exemption from filing.

arguments.justification: The statute defines "legislative agent" as one engaged "during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes," using a qualitative "main purposes" test rather than any numeric time percentage.

content.text:
I'll analyze each threshold question against the Ohio statute text.

The Ohio statute defines a "legislative agent" as someone engaged to actively advocate "as one of the individual's main purposes" - no specific compensation dollar threshold, no specific time percent threshold. Registration is triggered by engagement, not dollar amounts.

For itemization: §101.73(B)(3) requires itemized reporting of meals/food/beverages when cumulative payments to a particular official exceed $50 in a calendar year.

For expenditure registration threshold: there is no dollar threshold to register - registration is required within 10 days of engagement regardless of expenditure amount.
